Measured on `77f846a8b` while implementing the #5324 half (PR #5466). Three findings, and the card's own first question — "confirm whether the lazy path is reachable at all today" — now has an answer that changes what fixing this is worth.

## 1. The count is 46, and `index.tsx` is not the only cause

One console `vite build` emits **46** `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT` warnings, not "13+": 43 from `packages/fields` and 3 from `apps/console/src/pages/*` (`DocPage`, `DocsLayout`, `DocsSlug` — dynamically imported by `AppContent.tsx`, statically by `App.tsx`; app-internal, no public surface).

The card names `index.tsx` as the static importer. For 26 of the 43 there is a **second** one: `packages/fields/src/FieldEditWidget.tsx`, the grid's inline cell editor, which statically imports 24 widgets because a cell must edit synchronously. Removing the barrel's `export *` lines does not touch those warnings at all.

## 2. Fixing the barrel moves ZERO bytes

Measured, not inferred. Removing every `export * from './widgets/*.js'` whose module the barrel also lazy-imports, keeping only the ones in-repo code imports by name:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT` | 46 | 35 |
| eager closure, gzipped bytes | 3,881,609 | 3,881,938 |
| eager chunks | 58 | 58 |

The closure **grew by 329 bytes**. Nothing left it.

The reason is #5266's own mechanism, one level up from this file. `apps/console/vite.config.ts` declares an `advancedChunks` group named `ui-components` whose test matches `packages/(components|fields)`. Group assignment overrides a module's async-only reachability, so every `packages/fields` module is folded into one chunk — and that chunk is statically imported by the entry, because `packages/components` is. The `import()` calls in `index.tsx` are not defeated *only* by the static re-exports; they are defeated a second time by the chunking, and that second defeat survives any surgery on this file.

**The control that proves it:** `packages/fields/src/widgets/MarkdownContent.tsx` has a working `React.lazy` import, is re-exported by nothing, and has no static importer anywhere in the repo — the one widget whose laziness is *not* defeated by a static edge. It still lands in the eager `ui-components-*.js`. (Counter-probed: the same method reports `lazy` for the maplibre-gl and plugin-map chunks, so it is not stuck on one answer.)

So: the lazy path is reachable — `getLazyFieldWidget` is exported and app-shell's `ActionParamDialog` uses it — but in the console bundle it can never pay off while that chunk group stands.

## 3. It is a public-surface change, in-repo as well as published

Removing the re-exports failed the console build with 16 `MISSING_EXPORT` errors before it emitted a single warning (worth noting on its own: a warning count of **0** from that build meant the build died, not that the warnings were fixed).

14 widget classes are imported **by name** from `@object-ui/fields` by production code:

- `packages/plugin-detail/src/InlineFieldInput.tsx` — `AddressField`, `AvatarField`, `BooleanField`, `CurrencyField`, `FileField`, `GeolocationField`, `ImageField`, `LocationField`, `NumberField`, `PercentField`, `SelectField`, `SignatureField`, `UserField`
- `packages/plugin-form/src/{MasterDetailForm,LineItemsPanel}.tsx` and `apps/console/src/dev/DevLookup.tsx` — `LineItemsField` (via `GridField.js`)
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/FlowReferenceField.tsx` — `LookupField`

Plus two test files (`app-shell` on `SelectField`, `plugin-form` on `GridField`). And these are published exports of `@object-ui/fields`, so external consumers are affected too.

## What this card is actually deciding

Not "remove the static imports" — that is 11 fewer warnings and 0 fewer bytes, at the cost of a breaking change to `@object-ui/fields` plus a refactor of four production modules across three packages. On its own that trade is not worth taking.

The options, as they look after measuring:

- **A. Chunking first.** Stop `ui-components` from claiming `packages/fields/**` (or split fields out of that group) so a lazy widget can actually get its own chunk, then remove the defeating static edges. This is the only order in which the barrel work buys bytes. It needs its own measurement — the group exists to stop chunk explosion, and fields widgets are reached from many places.
- **B. Delete the decorative laziness.** Honest and cheap, but it deletes `getLazyFieldWidget`, which is public API and is used by `ActionParamDialog`.
- **C. Leave it and stop the warnings from reading as noise.** Cheapest, buys nothing.

I did not pick one — per the dispatch this is a stop-and-report, so `packages/fields` is untouched in PR #5466. The #5324 gauge that lands there now measures the closure, so whichever route is chosen, the bytes it moves will be visible for the first time.

## Premise falsified — moving to `needs-user-decision`

PM round 21, session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`. ⛔ Not a ruling and not a grading — recording the fork the measurement opened. The evidence is the dev's comment directly above; this note only moves the card's state and says why.

This card was dispatched folded with #5324 on the assumption that it was "the concrete half" — remove the defeating static re-exports, bytes leave the eager closure. **Measured, that is false in three independent ways:**

1. **Wrong target for most of it.** 26 of the 43 `packages/fields` warnings have a *second* static importer, `FieldEditWidget.tsx`, which must import synchronously because a grid cell edits in place. Barrel surgery does not touch them.
2. **Zero bytes.** Warnings 46 → 35, eager closure **+329 bytes**, chunks 58 → 58. Nothing left the closure.
3. **The real mechanism is one level up** — the `ui-components` `advancedChunks` group claims `packages/(components|fields)`, and group assignment overrides async-only reachability. Proven by a control widget (`MarkdownContent.tsx`) that has a working `React.lazy`, no re-export and no static importer anywhere, and still lands in the eager chunk. Counter-probed: the same method reports `lazy` for the maplibre and plugin-map chunks, so it is not stuck on one answer.

**And the fence held**: removing the re-exports is a real public-surface breach — 16 `MISSING_EXPORT` errors, 14 widget classes imported by name across `plugin-detail`, `plugin-form`, `app-shell` and `apps/console`, plus published exports of `@object-ui/fields` that external consumers rely on. The dev stopped rather than shipping it, which is what the dispatch required.

Worth keeping as a platform reading in its own right: **that failing build reported `0` warnings — because it died before emitting any, not because the warnings were fixed.** A zero from a warning count is not a reading until you know the build survived.

### Why this needs you rather than a seat

The three routes the dev laid out are not interchangeable, and **B is on the manual floor**: it deletes `getLazyFieldWidget`, which is published API and has a live consumer (`ActionParamDialog`). Deleting a released capability is a maintainer call, not a seat's. **A** (change the chunk group first, then remove the static edges) is the only order that buys bytes, but it needs its own measurement — the group exists to stop chunk explosion. **C** buys nothing and just stops the warnings reading as noise.

⛔ I am not choosing. Returning unassigned.

**One thing did improve regardless**: #5324 landed the eager-closure gauge, so whichever route is chosen, the bytes it moves will be measurable for the first time. Before today the entire question was invisible to CI.

The full decision inbox (46 cards) was presented with per-card four-axis recommendations; the maintainer accepted the batch, verbatim: 「接受所有」.

**Ruled:** Option C — de-noise now: leave the lazy/static import structure as it is (no barrel surgery, no public-surface breakage) and stop the 46 `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT` warnings from reading as noise in every console build. Option B (deleting `getLazyFieldWidget`, published API with a live consumer) is not taken. Option A — chunking first: stop the `ui-components` `advancedChunks` group from claiming `packages/fields/**` so lazy widgets can actually get their own chunks, then remove the defeating static edges — is retained as an on-hold measurement: it is the only order in which the barrel work buys bytes, but it needs its own measurement (the group exists to prevent chunk explosion) before any commitment, and the #5324 eager-closure gauge now makes that measurable.

State: `needs-user-decision` removed → `pm:queue` (ready for dispatch).

Clause-②: no — module graph and registration wiring; no authoring surface, no schema, no accept/reject behaviour. ⚠️ Flips to `yes` if the honest fix removes or renames a **published export** of `@object-ui/fields`; stop and report if it goes that way.
Serial constraints cleared: `packages/fields/**` — no in-flight claim in this lane. Concurrent siblings #5631 / #5853 (`packages/types` + `packages/components`), #5293 (`packages/plugin-view`), #5913 (`scripts/`) — all disjoint by full path.

## ⛔ Measure before you choose — the card names this explicitly and it is the ruling

> Someone should first confirm **whether the lazy path is reachable at all today**, before deciding whether to fix the laziness or delete it. Either outcome is an improvement over a dynamic import that silently does nothing.

**Both endings are acceptable deliveries.** ⛔ Do not decide first and measure afterwards; the answer changes which one is honest.

## The defect

Every console `vite build` emits a run of `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings: the same widget module has a **static** edge from `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` *and* an `import()` from the same importer, so it is in the eager graph regardless and the dynamic import is decoration. **13 named in one truncated log — treat that as a floor, not a total.**

The likely mechanism, stated as a PM assumption to test rather than a fact: the barrel statically imports each widget **in order to register it**, and the `React.lazy` path was added later without removing the eager registration. If that is right, the real question is **how the registry gets populated without the static imports** — which is why this is not a one-line fix.

⚠️ **The shape is not uniform, so do not treat the 13 as one batch.** The card measured two exceptions: `FileField` has **two** static importers (`index.tsx` *and* `widgets/GridField.tsx`), and `ImageCropperDialog` is dynamically imported by `ImageField.tsx` while statically imported by `index.tsx`. Each needs its own look; a uniform sweep would get those two wrong.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure these

1. **Get the real total.** The card's 13 came from a truncated log. Build and capture the full warning set; the number you report is the one that matters.
2. **Is the lazy path reachable at all?** If nothing can ever take it, deleting the `import()` calls is the honest fix and the bytes claim evaporates — say so plainly rather than engineering laziness nobody reaches.
3. **If it is reachable, measure the prize before paying for it.** These are heavy widgets (image cropping, grids, vector fields); #5266 is the sibling precedent where the same failure mode cost **~89 KiB gzipped on every page load** until someone measured it. An eager-closure reading before and after is the evidence that makes either ending defensible.
4. ⚠️ **AGENTS.md has a test-flakiness rule about module-scope imports of lazily-loaded modules in tests**, and the card names it as an interaction. Read it before restructuring the barrel — a fix that makes the graph right and the suite flaky is not a fix.

## Standing

⛔ Do not "fix" this by suppressing the warning. The warning text is currently **the only thing saying the laziness does not work**, and the card's second cost is precisely that it reads as noise. Silencing it without changing the graph would remove the signal and keep the defect — the worst of the three outcomes.

`premise_still_valid: false` with no PR is legitimate if the warnings are already gone. Use a control probe so a zero-hit build log reads as real.

Draft PR, `Fixes #5325`. Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders — the sanitizer eats them) and return it.

## ACCEPT — PR #6007 (R37, `domain:ui`)

Reviewed against the diff and `origin/main`.

### ⛔ First: my dispatch word was defective, and the defect was a skipped protocol step

**This card carried a maintainer ruling from 2026-08-22 — option C, verbatim 「接受所有」 — and my brief did not carry one word of it.** I verified it after your report: the ruling is on the card, and so is the round-21 note that already falsified the premise, already identified the `advancedChunks` mechanism, and already ran the `MarkdownContent` control.

So my brief:
- quoted the card's stale *"13 named in one truncated log"* when the measured figure was already 43/46;
- **re-asked "is the lazy path reachable at all?"** — a question round 21 answered in writing;
- issued a prohibition (*"do not fix this by suppressing the warning"*) that sat in tension with the ruling's own instruction to stop the warnings reading as noise.

**Cause, stated plainly: I read this card's body and never read its comments.** I ran the decision re-read on the round's other four cards; this one I added late as a substitute for #5980 and dispatched on the body alone. That is the exact step that caught three separate errors for me earlier today, skipped on the one card added under time pressure. Recorded in the seat post as a hard rule with no "unless the card looks simple" clause.

You found the ruling yourself and implemented it. That is the second time today a dev has recovered a dispatch I under-briefed.

### Both open questions — ruled A

**Q1, the fence extension: accepted.** I verified all three legs of your argument on `origin/main`:

- `apps/console/vite.config.ts:99` `assertLazyLinterStaysLazy` and `:229` `emitEagerClosureReport`, both registered at `:568`/`:574` — the two sibling guards of this exact genre already live in that file;
- `:660` — `{ name: 'ui-components', test: /packages[\\/](components|fields)[\\/]/, priority: 80 }`, the group that overrides async-only reachability;
- `:60` and `:176` — that file's *own comments* already document the mechanism.

My fence was copied from the card's file list, and the card names `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` because that is where the *defect* is. But the **ruled fix is a property of the console bundle graph**, and `packages/fields`' own build emits none of these warnings. The fence could not hold the ruling. ⛔ Option C (relocating the ledger under `packages/fields`) is worse, and your reason is right: it would put a console-specific ratchet inside a published package.

**Q2, checked ledger vs suppression: A, and it is the only reading under which both instructions hold.** My prohibition targeted *deleting the signal*. What shipped **strengthens** it: an unpinned sighting keeps rolldown's original text verbatim **and fails the build**, and a pinned entry that stops firing **also** fails it. Under my literal reading (leave all 43 printing), a 44th widget joins the list tomorrow in total silence. Under yours, that is a red build. You built the reconciliation instead of choosing a side, which was the right instinct.

### The counter-probe is the part that makes this a gate

> a build that dies before chunk assignment emits no warnings at all … a build killed by 16 `MISSING_EXPORT` errors reported `0` … which reads identically to "fixed"

That trap is recorded on this very card from round 21, and the `missing` half of the diff is what disarms it: **a blind build now fails with 43 named absences instead of a clean-looking zero.** Checking the *dangerous* direction — where zero is the suspicious reading, not the reassuring one — is what separates this from a filter with extra steps.

Three more things worth naming:

- **`MarkdownContent.tsx`'s absence from the ledger is itself an assertion**, with a test enforcing it. It has working `React.lazy`, no static importer, emits no warning — **and still lands in the eager chunk**. That is what proves the second defeat is chunking, not imports, and it is why barrel surgery moves zero bytes. Counter-probed against `plugin-map`/`plugin-charts`/`plugin-report` reporting `lazy`, so `EAGER` is not a stuck answer.
- **The failure wording is unit-tested** — *"the number to distrust is the zero"* — with the reason stated: "a maintainer who reads 'did not fire' as 'fixed' deletes 43 lines and switches the check off." Pinning the sentence that keeps a gate alive is unusual and correct.
- **Static importers are deliberately NOT pinned.** "They churn with ordinary refactors, and a gate that fires on an unrelated PR with a message about somebody else's card is how a gate gets switched off." That is a real design judgement about gate survival, not a shortcut.

Byte-neutrality is measured, not assumed: eager closure identical at **3,310,419** gzipped, 52/508 chunks, before and after. Empty-frontmatter changeset is the right call — build tooling only, no published source moved.

### One process note for the record

Your ablation's `EXIT/INT/TERM` trap **fired but resolved its path from the wrong cwd**, so you completed the restore manually and verified it (grep back to 1, `git status` clean) before the final build. Reported rather than papered over — and it is the *second distinct way* these restore traps have failed today: #3909's fired **between** bash invocations and silently measured an unmutated tree. Both go into the seat post; a trap is not a restore until the restore is verified.

### Landing

Not governed (`apps/console/**` and `scripts/**` are not on the governed path list). Gates read **by name, once**, at ~11 min past this PR's own run `started_at`; enqueue requires **every** check green, not the required subset.

⚠️ Carried forward: **option A remains on hold by the ruling** — stop the `ui-components` group claiming `packages/fields/**`, *then* remove the defeating static edges. Your side observation that `vendor-markdown-*.js` sits in the eager closure at **164,708 gzipped bytes**, with `MarkdownContent`'s overridden laziness as one reason, is a concrete place to point that measurement when it is taken. Recorded here rather than filed, since the ruling already tracks option A.
